Boxoffy Editorial · Week 3 · Apr 13–19, 2026
BEEF S2 Leads. South India Arrives. Euphoria Divides. JioHotstar + SonyLIV Get Deeper.
BEEF Season 2 takes the top spot on Netflix India in its debut week — and it earns it. The anthology gamble paid off. Oscar Isaac and Cailee Spaeny in a country-club power war is exactly the kind of prestige television Indian urban audiences have been starved of since the original BEEF. The move to anthology format, widely criticised before release, is now the thing people are talking about in its favour. The bigger India story this week is South cinema's OTT moment: Ustaad Bhagat Singh and Youth both landed on Netflix within 24 hours of each other. Both debuted in the top 5. Pan-India theatrical carry-over is real and the streaming numbers will confirm it. Euphoria Season 3 is this week's most-watched argument. 44% on Rotten Tomatoes is the lowest in franchise history — but it's still #1 globally on HBO Max. In India, the premium urban audience is watching and debating. That's not disappointment; that's engagement. JioHotstar, ZEE5 and SonyLIV now show full top 5s this week. That reveals three structural patterns Netflix-first coverage always misses. On JioHotstar, Warner Bros' Project Hail Mary hitting India OTT 46 days after theatrical is the fastest Hollywood tentpole window to Jio since Dune 2 — signalling WB's confidence that the 500M+ reach moves the needle on long-tail film economics. Saiyaara's Tier-2 Hindi-belt pull on JioHotstar (W3 library lift) confirms musical-romance has a second commercial life on OTT that action cinema structurally doesn't. On SonyLIV, Shark Tank India S4's 2.4 TVT BARC Week 15 reading is the only OTT title in India with officially-validated dual-measurement; the TVF pairing of Kota Factory S4 + Gullak S5 + Rocket Boys S3 makes SonyLIV the most critically-defensible Hindi originals slate of 2026 even as its raw reach lags. On ZEE5, the 72-week library hold of Freedom at Midnight and the 6-week sustain of Sultan of Delhi S3 show ZEE5's period-drama + crime-franchise positioning is doing exactly what ZEE bet on: low-churn, high-loyalty viewership from audiences Netflix/Prime under-serve. Monday hold for Matka King and Assi will be the week's key data watch.

Boxoffy Methodology · How We Track OTT India
5 Signals We Triangulate · No Single Source Ever Wins
India's OTT measurement is a patchwork. Netflix + Prime publish official watch hours selectively. JioHotstar, ZEE5, SonyLIV publish nothing. So every ranking on this page is a weighted blend of 5 independent signals — each disclosed below, each with its own bias and use-case.
Ormax
OTT Intelligence
Weekly OTT audience estimates across 25+ platforms. Panel-based modelling of 50,000+ Indian households. Weighted highest (0.85) in BCM-OTT for reach measurement. Tier-1 + Tier-2 coverage; Tier-3 under-represented.
Weight: 0.85 · Coverage: All platforms
BARC
TV Proxy · Hindi GEC
Broadcast Audience Research Council India. Doesn't measure OTT directly. But for titles with TV simulcast (Shark Tank India → Sony SAB, Doordarshan reruns, GEC-adjacent programming), BARC TVTs serve as validated BARC-linked proxy. Most rigorous data source on this page when applicable.
Weight: 1.00 · Coverage: Simulcast titles only
X Scans
Signal · Engagement
India-geo Twitter/X trending data per show hashtag. Discussion volume, peak trending rank, sentiment split. Captures demographic + metropolitan skew. Weak for rural mass pull (where X penetration is low), strong for premium/urban engagement reads. Useful qualitatively, not quantitatively.
Weight: 0.40 · Coverage: All titles
FlixPatrol
Popularity · Global
Country-by-country popularity score derived from Top 10 appearances on each platform. Best signal for Netflix (scraped public top 10) and Prime Video. Weaker for JioHotstar/ZEE5/SonyLIV because these platforms don't publish public top 10 scoreboards.
Weight: 0.75 (NF/Prime) · 0.30 (others)
Official
Platform Disclosures
Netflix Tudum hours (weekly Tuesdays). Prime Video press releases. Occasional HBO Max statements. When available, these override all other signals. Marked with ✓ green across this page. Only ~12% of titles ever get official numbers.
Weight: 1.00 · Coverage: ~12% of titles
How the weighting works · Boxoffy OTT Canonical Model
For each ranked title, the India Rank reflects: (a) Ormax OTT estimate, normalised for platform reach; (b) FlixPatrol popularity score where applicable; (c) X-India trending peak × sentiment; (d) BARC TVT when a TV simulcast exists; and (e) platform-official disclosures when published. When signals disagree, we disclose the range. When only one signal is available (typical for JioHotstar/ZEE5/SonyLIV titles), the single source is named explicitly in the row note. We never blend signals without attribution. Every ranking on this page can be audited against the 5 inputs above.
